$comment: PROJECT hooks for the Human Battery Project agent organization.
Build order step 1.
ONE hook, registered on every tool that can put bytes into a file, plus
Bash. Bash is on the list because Bash is the hole in the other layer: an
agent with no Edit can still run `sed -i`, a heredoc or `cp`.
WHAT THE HOOK USES TO TELL AGENTS APART. `agent_type` on the payload,
supplied by the harness. It is not an environment variable and not
anything the agent writes, so an agent cannot set its own name. It is
ABSENT in the main conversation, which is the chain of command written
down: canon, legal text and the mark belong to the person directing this
work, and his session is not an agent.
IT FAILS CLOSED. A payload the hook cannot parse is a write whose target
it cannot see. An unexpected exception is reported as a refusal and never
as an allowance. That is the opposite of the usual choice and it is
deliberate: the hook is registered only for writes.
THE HOOK IS THE SECOND LAYER, NOT THE FIRST. The first is the `tools:`
line in each agent file. A read-only agent has no Edit and no Write at
all. Neither layer is weakened to make the other convenient.
Proof:  python3 .claude/hooks/protected-paths.py --seed
python3 .claude/hooks/tests/test_protected_paths.py
49 cases, 31 refusals, 18 allowances and 3 fail-closed, from the
run and not from a plan. Wired into .githooks/pre-commit.
